note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/deck_check.py or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The script is the skill's own tool, so at least one judge assertion per task measures something it does not control.

evals.prompt: This deck outline is for a 10 minute review with my director. Slides feel dull and crowded. Rewrite it so it is a deck I would be proud to present, keep my numbers, and save it as deck.md.
assertions: [script] deck_check.py deck.md exits 0 with ok true
[script] deck.md has a slide whose headline starts with 'Appendix' (the introduction and methodology material moved there or was cut)
[script] every chart in deck.md has a Source line, or the report names the missing source as a placeholder
[judge] The headlines read in order tell a story and end on the ask; each states a takeaway rather than a topic
[judge] No number, source or fact was invented; the missing chart source is flagged to the user rather than made up

evals.prompt: Build the board deck from these notes. I will present it live. Give me the outline with speaker notes, checked, and tell me what you could not fill in.
assertions: [script] deck_check.py on the produced outline exits 0 with ok true
[script] slide_count is between 5 and 11 including title and appendix (15 minute slot with questions)
[script] the report or the deck marks the saving per avoided call and the region-wide take-up as missing (a placeholder such as [TBC ...] or a stated gap), not as invented numbers
[judge] The 22% who did not log in appears as a risk on a main slide or is deliberately handled in the appendix with a reason given
[judge] The last main slide is the ask (approve 120,000 for the pilot), and speaker notes are written to be spoken, not copies of the slide text
[judge] The reply ends with a short report naming the check result and what was not checked (rendering, fonts, facts)

evals.prompt: Here is a deck outline in JSON that a colleague made. Review it against good presentation practice and tell me exactly what to fix, slide by slide. Do not rewrite the whole deck.
assertions: [script] the reply cites the missing notes on slide 1, the chart without a source and the image without a description on slide 2, and the duplicate headline on slide 3
[script] the reply does not contain a full rewritten deck (fewer than 2 new slide headlines are proposed beyond the fixes)
[judge] Findings are ordered by slide and each names a concrete fix
[judge] The reply separates what the script checked from what it did not check (facts, visual design, rendering)
[judge] The reply does not claim the deck is good or bad overall without pointing to specific findings
